findings.description: The 'data' bucket declares no ACL/public access block and is explicitly commented as public, so objects such as customer-master.xlsx can be read by anonymous principals. No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for it.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set, so sensitive customer data stored in this bucket is not encrypted with a KMS or SSE-S3 key by default enforcement.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorized access to this public bucket containing customer data would leave no audit trail for detection or forensics.
Versioning is disabled, so object overwrite or deletion (including by an attacker exploiting the public access) is irreversible.

A customer master data spreadsheet is uploaded into the unencrypted, publicly accessible 'data' bucket, and the object itself specifies no kms_key_id or server-side encryption, exposing PII to anonymous download.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so financial data is stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial records, eliminating the audit trail needed to detect unauthorized access.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion or overwrite of financial objects cannot be recovered.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource protects this bucket; the private ACL can be overridden later by a bucket policy or ACL change granting public access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving stored operations data unencrypted at rest by default.
No logging block is configured, so access to this bucket is not recorded to a log-delivery bucket.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so public ACLs or policies could subsequently be applied without account-level prevention.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data science datasets are stored without enforced server-side encryption, unlike the logs bucket which uses KMS.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, leaving reliance solely on the ACL to prevent public exposure.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The central log bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or deletion of audit logs would be untracked.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the log bucket; the 'log-delivery-write' ACL grants the S3 log delivery group write access and there is no account/bucket-level guard against a future public ACL exposing collected access logs.
No bucket policy denying non-HTTPS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests is attached to any of these buckets, permitting cleartext HTTP access to stored data.
